fields.mechanism: Flared self‑expanding metal stent that exerts outward radial force to keep a conduit open, a principle used in expandable pipe supports in the oil & gas industry.
fields.intervention: Integrate a self‑expanding metal mesh sleeve around the floor lumen of the drainage catheter that flares outward to maintain a larger cross‑section and resist collapse/occlusion.
fields.expected_effect: Prevents lumen narrowing and maintains consistent drainage flow, improving reliability of multi‑lumen catheters.
fields.falsification_test: Apply compressive loads to the catheter in a mechanical tester and record the lumen diameter and flow rate before and after loading, comparing to a conventional catheter.

fields.mechanism: Radial expansion of a flared self‑expanding metal stent creates a permanent, patent conduit that resists external compression and maintains lumen openness, allowing passive fluid flow through any inserted catheter.
fields.intervention: Integrate a flared self‑expanding metal stent segment into the wall of the multi‑lumen drainage catheter, using the stent’s mesh pores (≥ 4 mm) to house the catheter’s drainage lumen, thereby providing a passive, structurally supported pathway that resists occlusion.
fields.expected_effect: The catheter’s drainage lumen remains continuously patent, reducing or eliminating lumen occlusion and preserving flow without reliance on active flushing.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a bench‑top study comparing flow rate stability and occlusion incidence over 7 days between standard multi‑lumen catheters and catheters modified with the integrated flared self‑expanding metal stent segment under simulated physiological pressures and debris load.

fields.mechanism: Radial outward force of a flared self‑expanding metal stent that keeps the lumen open and prevents occlusion
fields.intervention: Integrate a short flared self‑expanding metal mesh segment into the catheter wall, creating a ≥4 mm mesh aperture through which one drainage lumen passes, so the stent’s radial force maintains that lumen’s patency
fields.expected_effect: The targeted lumen remains patent despite debris or tissue ingrowth, reducing occlusion and preserving consistent flow without additional moving parts
fields.falsification_test: In a bench‑top model with viscous, particulate‑laden fluid, measure flow rate and time‑to‑occlusion for catheters with the integrated mesh segment versus standard catheters; a statistically significant longer patency time confirms the mechanism

fields.mechanism: Radial expansion of a self‑expanding metal stent that provides a rigid scaffold and a mesh pore for catheter insertion, combining mechanical support with fluidic drainage to maintain lumen patency.
fields.intervention: Integrate a flared self‑expanding metal stent segment into the multi‑lumen drainage catheter, creating a dedicated larger‑diameter mesh aperture through which a wider floor lumen is threaded, forming a combined stent‑catheter conduit.
fields.expected_effect: The mechanical scaffold prevents lumen collapse and occlusion, while the wider floor lumen positioned through the mesh maintains continuous fluid flow, reducing lumen occlusion events.
fields.falsification_test: In a bench‑top simulated drainage model, compare flow rates and occlusion frequency between standard catheters and catheters with the integrated stent‑mesh scaffold under cyclic compression and bio‑film formation; a statistically significant reduction in occlusion confirms the mechanism.

fields.mechanism: A flared self‑expanding metal stent expands to maintain lumen patency and its mesh pores provide a protected conduit through which a drainage catheter can be threaded, creating a combined stent‑catheter channel that resists occlusion.
fields.intervention: Integrate a flared self‑expanding metal stent within the multi‑lumen drainage catheter and thread a wider floor lumen catheter through a ≥4 mm mesh pore of the stent, forming a PTCD‑Stent complex that preserves sterility.
fields.expected_effect: The combined stent‑catheter conduit remains open despite debris, restoring and sustaining flow while preventing lumen occlusion and maintaining a sterile barrier.
fields.falsification_test: In a sterile bench model simulating viscous fluid and particulate debris, compare flow rate decay and occlusion frequency between a standard multi‑lumen catheter and one equipped with the flared self‑expanding stent‑mesh‑pore catheter configuration over 72 hours.
